deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It sits between two pages of combinatorics of 2-dimensional pseudo-line arrangements (bigons, the types I_N, II_4, II_5, III_6, IV_7, and 'lattice-like' or cellular arrangements), but it is a German-language personal and meditative draft that appears to have been interleaved in the folder.

In modern paraphrase, Grothendieck considers how to proceed with a self-examination of his life. Key points:
- He might follow rising memories ('aufsteigende Erinnerungen') or also take up later periods of his life, without waiting for some further trigger.
- What matters most is the 'complete spontaneity of the investigation'.
- In that same spirit, he could start from any period of his life, perhaps using a rich body of material such as a correspondence with 'M...k' since 1942.
- The right column seems to continue with a relationship he had 'until her death', which he says he has never examined closely.
- Taking up this 'Stoff' (material) first would be a kind of hinge ('Scharnier') between the work of the past 'seven months' and the work ahead of him.
- It could give an Ariadne's thread ('Ariane-faden') leading further back into his childhood, or forward into his adult life.
- The page breaks off with: 'But before I engage in depth with any period or question concerning my life...'.

The feminine 'bis zu ihrem Tod' together with 'since 1942' (the year he was separated from his mother at Rieucros and sent to Le Chambon-sur-Lignon) makes it plausible that the correspondence is with his mother, Hanka Grothendieck, who died in 1957. This is an inference from context; the name is not legible. The page belongs to Grothendieck's introspective writing of the late 1970s and 1980s (the 'méditation' genre), not to the pseudo-line notes.
